sentences.en: Last week, we started looking at reptiles, including crocodiles and snakes.
sentences.zh: 上周，我们开始了解爬行动物，包括鳄鱼和蛇。

sentences.en: Today, I'd like us to have a look at another reptile - the lizard - and in particular, at some studies that have been done on a particular type of lizard whose Latin name is tiliqua is rugosa.
sentences.zh: 今天，我想带大家了解另一种爬行动物——蜥蜴，特别是针对一种学名为Tiliqua rugosa的蜥蜴所开展的一些研究。

sentences.en: This is commonly known as the sleepy lizard, because it's quite slow in its movements and spends quite a lot of its time dozing under rocks or lying in the sun.
sentences.zh: 这种蜥蜴通常被称为‘瞌睡蜥蜴’，因为它行动十分缓慢，且大部分时间都在岩石下打盹或在阳光下躺着。

sentences.en: I'll start with a general description.
sentences.zh: 我先从总体描述开始。

sentences.en: Sleepy lizards live in Western and South Australia, where they're quite common.
sentences.zh: 瞌睡蜥蜴生活在西澳大利亚州和南澳大利亚州，在当地相当常见。

sentences.en: Unlike European lizards, which are mostly small, green and fast- moving, sleepy lizards are brown, but what's particularly distinctive about them is the colour of 031 their tongue, which is dark blue, in contrast with the lining of their mouth which is bright pink.
sentences.zh: 与主要体型小、呈绿色且行动迅速的欧洲蜥蜴不同，瞌睡蜥蜴呈棕色，而其最显著的特征是舌头的颜色——深蓝色，与其口腔内壁鲜明的粉红色形成强烈对比。

sentences.en: And they're much bigger than most European lizards.
sentences.zh: 此外，它们的体型也比大多数欧洲蜥蜴大得多。

sentences.en: They have quite a varied diet, including insects and even small animals, but they mostly eat plants of varying kinds.
sentences.zh: 它们的食谱相当多样，包括昆虫甚至小型动物，但主要以各类植物为食。

sentences.en: Even though they're quite large and powerful, with strong jaws that can crush beetles and snail shells, they still have a quite a few predators.
sentences.zh: 尽管它们体型较大、力量较强，拥有能压碎甲虫和蜗牛壳的强健颌骨，却仍有不少天敌。

sentences.en: Large birds like cassowaries were one of the main ones in the past, but nowadays they're more likely to be caught and killed by snakes.
sentences.zh: 过去，像鹤鸵这样的大型鸟类曾是其主要天敌之一；但如今，它们更可能被蛇捕获并杀死。

sentences.en: Actually, another threat to their survival isn't a predator at all, but is man-made - quite a large number of sleepy lizards are killed by cars when they're trying to cross highways.
sentences.zh: 事实上，对它们生存构成的另一威胁根本不是天敌，而是人为因素——大量瞌睡蜥蜴在试图穿越高速公路时被车辆撞死。

sentences.en: One study carried out by Michael Freake at Flinders University investigated the methods of navigation of these lizards.
sentences.zh: 弗林德斯大学的迈克尔·弗里克（Michael Freake）开展了一项研究，调查了这些蜥蜴的导航方式。

sentences.en: Though they move slowly, they can travel quite long distances.
sentences.zh: 尽管它们移动缓慢，却能行进相当长的距离。

sentences.en: And he found that even if they were taken some distance away from their home territory, they could usually find their way back home as long as they could see the sky - they didn't need any other landmarks on the ground.
sentences.zh: 他发现，即使将它们带到远离其栖息地的远处，只要能看到天空，它们通常都能找到回家的路——并不需要地面其他任何地标。

sentences.en: Observations of these lizards in the wild have also revealed that their mating habits are quite unusual.
sentences.zh: 野外观察还揭示出，这些蜥蜴的交配习性相当特殊。

sentences.en: Unlike most animals, it seems that they're relatively monogamous, returning to the same partner year after year.
sentences.zh: 与大多数动物不同，它们似乎具有相对稳定的单配偶制倾向，年复一年地回到同一伴侣身边。

sentences.en: And the male and female also stay together for a long time, both before and after the birth of their young.
sentences.zh: 雄性和雌性不仅在幼崽出生前后长期共同生活，彼此陪伴的时间也很长。

sentences.en: It's quite interesting to think about the possible reasons for this.
sentences.zh: 思考这一现象的潜在原因颇为有趣。

sentences.en: It could be that it's to do with protecting their young - you'd expect them to have a much better chance of survival if they have both parents around.
sentences.zh: 一种可能是为了保护后代——人们会预期，若双亲都在身边，幼崽的存活几率会高得多。

sentences.en: But in fact observers have noted that once the babies have Audioscripts hatched out of their eggs, they have hardly any contact with their parents.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，观察者注意到，幼崽破壳而出后，几乎不再与父母有任何接触。

sentences.en: So, there's not really any evidence to support that idea.
sentences.zh: 因此，这一观点实际上缺乏确凿证据支持。

sentences.en: Another suggestion's based on the observation that male lizards in monogamous relationships tend to be bigger and stronger than other males.
sentences.zh: 另一种推测基于一项观察：处于单配偶关系中的雄性蜥蜴，往往比其他雄性体型更大、更强壮。

sentences.en: So maybe the male lizards stay around so they can give the female lizards protection from other males.
sentences.zh: 因此，雄性蜥蜴或许留在雌性身边，是为了保护雌性免受其他雄性的侵扰。

sentences.en: But again, we're not really sure.
sentences.zh: 但同样，我们对此尚无定论。

sentences.en: Finally, I'd like to mention another study that involved collecting data by tracking the lizards.
sentences.zh: 最后，我想提一下另一项研究，该研究通过追踪蜥蜴来收集数据。

sentences.en: I was actually involved in this myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己也曾参与其中。

sentences.en: So we caught some lizards in the wild and we developed a tiny GPS system that would allow us to track them, and we fixed this onto their tails.
sentences.zh: 我们于野外捕捉了一些蜥蜴，并研发了一套微型GPS系统，可用来追踪它们的活动，然后将其固定在蜥蜴尾巴上。

sentences.en: Then we set the lizards free again, and we were able to track them for twelve days and gather data, not just about their location, but even about how many steps they took during this period.
sentences.zh: 随后我们将蜥蜴重新放归野外，并持续追踪了十二天，不仅收集了它们的位置信息，甚至记录了此期间它们所走的步数。

sentences.en: One surprising thing we discovered from this is that there were far fewer meetings between lizards than we expected - it seems that they were actually trying to avoid one another.
sentences.zh: 这项研究中一个令人惊讶的发现是：蜥蜴之间的相遇次数远少于我们的预期——它们似乎实际上在刻意回避彼此。

sentences.en: So why would that be?
sentences.zh: 那么，这又是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, again we have no clear evidence, but one hypothesis is that male lizards can cause quite serious injuries to one another, so maybe this avoidance is a way of preventing this - of self-preservation, if you like.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们目前并无明确证据，但一种假说是：雄性蜥蜴相互之间可能造成相当严重的伤害，因此这种回避行为或许是一种防止此类伤害发生的自我保护机制。

sentences.en: But we need to collect a lot more data before we can be sure of any of this.
sentences.zh: 但在得出任何确切结论之前，我们还需收集大量更多数据。
